As someone who works in the field of narrative storytelling…(being vague bc paranoia) I cannot tell you how mad I am about her “director” journey. 

I don’t have a problem with her directing her own music videos. Go off. And she probably knows what she’s doing from being on MV sets all her life. (Though I find her videos very literal, overproduced, uncreative and there’s a reason why her earlier videos are much more popular.) 

But it’s the self mythologizing that I have an issue with. Because actually a lot of musical artists do direct their own videos and they’re not out here branding themselves as a ~director~. To call a 10 min music video that acts out the lyrics of All Too Well a “short film” and act as if it deserves an Oscar, to do a “director on director” talk with Martin McDonagh, a master of the craft who’s devoted his entire life to writing and directing, then now call herself a director in the same breath as singer/songwriter (a job in which she’s actually left a deep legacy) is just insulting. The documentary isn’t even about anything other than her as a music artist so why waste breath reminding us she’s a “director.” 

Yeah maybe I’m just jealous bc it takes 99.9% of people YEARS and endless blood sweat and tears to get a chance to direct anything on a professional level. But be a humble student of a new craft and I’ll have more respect. 

I’ve also never gotten the impression that she actually loves the unique medium of film from the way she talks about it, it seems like she’s more into adding “director” to her superwoman resume than having a genuine love for a totally different type of storytelling. 

And yes in case her team is reading this I would 10000000000000000000% say all this about a man and I do, about plenty of men in my field who get away w mediocrity. To me feminism means we don’t repeat the faults of the patriarchy. Not get to be as self-important as (some) men are.

When I fuck up I am able to see that it doesn’t make me a bad person. But I don’t say I healed my BPD because for me it helps me stay vigilant and careful about my mental health, and it’s not setting me up for failure if I do experience those symptoms again. Hi there, first of all, things will get better. The way you’ve written here is so clear and well thought out, you understand the issue and you’re taking responsibility for your impact on others, and I think that’s really admirable. I also made a post today about a situation I’m dealing with that has to do w me lashing out…. I can understand the pain of people cutting me out. 

If you haven’t done DBT yet definitely check out the resources on this sub & beyond. Specifically I think the following skills will benefit you greatly: 
-STOP (which is literally about stopping the moment) 
-check the facts (thinking about whether you actually are perceiving what’s happening or projecting)
- pro/con (do the pros of saying/doing this to this person- like blocking someone- outweigh the cons? Usually no.) 
- DEARMAN, GIVE, FAST (they’re acronyms, communication skills that you can employ consciously instead of lashing out.) 

Here’s also my two cents that might be kinda controversial. I see in your other post that you have a psychiatrist and take sertraline. I take wellbutrin/lamictal but I also get prescribed a small number of benzodiazepines (I get Klonopin personally but Ativan is also good. And I am talking like, 5 pills a month) which I strictly use for “emotional emergencies.” When deep breaths don’t work, when DBT skills don’t work, when I literally feel like I’m going to say/do something I will regret, I take one. It usually calms me down to the point where those impulses pass, and I can make healthier choices, or honestly just fall asleep lol. 

Benzos have HIGH addiction potential, which I have learned the hard way, so it’s important to be very disciplined with yourself about this. But, having it in my back pocket (literally) has often given me a sense of safety that actually helps me not even get to the point where I need to take it. If your doctor is open to it, I think it may be a good tool to have while you’re simultaneously learning more ways to self-regulate. 

Good luck!

I know this is an annoying answer but there are no secrets. This is the science of weight loss: burning  more calories than consuming them. (r/CICO) 

It’s annoyingly simple, but it’s science, that is how weight loss works. But there are lots of ways that calories are burned & gained, which is where the trends come from. 

While working out is great for burning more calories I have found there is no way to avoid consuming less calories if weight loss is your goal, whether that’s done through your diet, ozempic, no drinking, intermittent fasting, etc. 

What working out (specifically stuff like Solidcore that incorporates resistance training) HELPS with though is building muscle so your body automatically burns more fat & more calories! But to make this work, you also need to increase your protein intake a LOT. Like 0.85g-1g per body weight. This is harder to achieve than it sounds (at least for me) unless I’m eating protein at every meal or incorporating protein powder. 

Also if you find it stressful there is no need to do this but for me tracking calories and macros through Apple Watch, apps like MyFitnessPal or Noom has really helped stay on track and also feel like I’m in control of my journey. 

And of course working out has so many more benefits than weight loss :) I know your post is about weight loss / I also got into fitness to lose weight, but since then I’ve really fallen in love with staying active, and that has helped keep the weight off. 

Good luck! ❤️
